Title: Chasing Shadows

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

A warm, sunlit living room filled with trinkets and family photos. A familiar hum of a functioning household. MRS. WALLACE (early 50s, comforting presence) sits in a plush armchair, knitting. Her husband, MR. WALLACE (early 50s, stern yet loving) enters, carrying the day's newspaper.

MR. WALLACE
(disapproving)
What's this, dear? Another day of idleness?

MRS. WALLACE
(smiling)
I'm making a blanket for the baby, dear.

MR. WALLACE
(sighs)
And what's LUCAS doing these days? He's growing up so fast.

MRS. WALLACE
(worried)
He's just practicing for the school play, dear. He's very focused on it.

MR. WALLACE
(frustrated)
Focused? Or obsessed? He doesn't need to be a star.

INT. LUCAS'S BEDROOM - LATER

A cluttered room filled with posters of famous actors. LUCAS (12, intense, ambitious) sits in front of a mirror practicing his lines. His mother knocks on the door.

MRS. WALLACE
(concerned)
Lucas, dear, it's time for dinner.

LUCAS
(distracted)
Just a minute, mom.

INT. DINNER TABLE - NIGHT

The Wallace family shares a meal in the cozy dining room. MR. WALLACE stares at his son with disappointment.

MR. WALLACE
(disappointed)
You're not touching your food, Lucas.

LUCAS
(defiant)
I'm saving myself for the big night.

MR. WALLACE
(frustrated)
The school play? That's not an excuse to neglect your health, son.

INT. LUCAS'S SCHOOL - DAY

Lucas, decked out in a theater costume, rehearses with his classmates. Mr. Thompson, the theater teacher, watches with approval.

MR. THOMPSON
(encouraging)
Lucas, you have a natural talent. Keep at it.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Mrs. Wallace sits on the couch, reading a book. Lucas enters, looking distressed.

LUCAS
(frustrated)
I can't do it, mom. I can't remember my lines.

MRS. WALLACE
(comforting)
It's okay, Lucas. You'll get it. We'll practice together.

INT. THEATER - NIGHT

The big night arrives. Lucas stands on stage, eyes wide with fear and excitement. The spotlight illuminates him as he delivers his lines flawlessly. The audience, including his proud parents, claps and cheers.

INT. LIVING ROOM - MORNING

The Wallace family gathers around the breakfast table, exhausted but elated. Lucas's achievement brings the family closer together.

MR. WALLACE
(smiling)
I guess you can be a star, Lucas.

FADE OUT.

---

END OF SCREENPLAY.
